_meta.purpose: Master JSON template + permanent rulebook for the Long Video Generator planner (Gemini fills it, Python validates it, FFmpeg renders it).

probe.audio: AAC 44.1 kHz stereo, runs 0-163.28 s only

derived_from.note: Everything after 187.5 s is a set of example clips for the owner's notes (letterboxed, other creators). They are excluded from every statistic below.
methods: frame-level cut detection (colour histogram + tiny-gray diff, cross-checked by a second detector)
OCR of the owner's on-screen notes

measured.transitions: All 52 boundaries are hard cuts: no flashes, fades or dissolves found. One possible fast push-in with blur on the last ~4 frames before the intro-to-main cut (moderate confidence).
measured.slow_motion: No evidence: 0.2% duplicated frames, no freeze runs.
measured.letterbox: None. The edit itself is full-frame 16:9.

beat_sync.verdict: Cuts are NOT beat-locked in the reference. Beat placement stays optional.

measured.wide_share_estimate: about 20% of main (by eye from 37 sampled frames; low confidence)
measured.intro_to_main_pattern: intro ends on a player close-up, then a 0.73 s wide shot, then the close-up of the same action (4.43 s).

owner_spec_vs_reference: LETTERBOX: owner spec asks for a 2:1 block with black bars; the reference edit has none. Spec followed (render_spec.letterbox.enabled=true). Set it to false to match the reference.

LETTERBOX FILTER: the filter as written leaves 16:9 footage un-barred and crashes on vertical footage (tested). A corrected filter with an added crop is used. The original is kept in render_spec.letterbox.filter_as_written.
FPS: the reference is 30 fps; spec says 60. Spec followed. 24/25/30 fps sources get duplicated frames, not new motion.
LENGTH: the reference music is 163.28 s but its visuals run 187.5 s. Rule: final length = audible end of the music; section sizes scale by share.
PACING: the reference is moderate (main median 3.55 s), not very fast. Follow the measured distribution.
TEXT: the reference carries on-screen notes for the AI. The final render never has any text.

letterbox.note: Scale-to-cover then centre-crop: no stretching, no squashing. Costs the top and bottom 11% of a 16:9 frame.

shot_id.description: S001, S002 ... in playback order, no gaps.

source_video_file.description: Exact file name from the provided list. Never invent one.

trim_start.description: Seconds into the source where the clip starts.

duration.description: Seconds this clip occupies on the output timeline.

transition.description: How the cut INTO this shot looks. zoom_punch_cut = quick push-in with blur on the last 0.15 s of the previous clip, then a hard cut.

speed_multiplier.description: 1.0 = real time. Source seconds used = duration x speed_multiplier.

speed.note: Hard schema range is 0.5-1.5; values outside 0.8-1.0 raise a warning.

global: G1 The video is intro, then main, then outro. Nothing else. The video ends with the outro.
G2 Video length equals the music. Section sizes scale by share, with the intro held to 15-20 s on normal-length videos.
G3 Use only file names from the provided list and only windows that exist inside those files.
G5 No text, titles, labels or end cards on the video.
G6 When footage runs short, drop optional clip types first (goal, face, pass) and say so. Never invent footage.

rules: I1 Start with a bus-arrival scene. If none exists, start with the target player coming out of the bus or tunnel.
I2 Then dressing-room clips (the player's jersey or his moment in the dressing room) and a little fan footage if any.
I3 Use at most one celebration clip, and only to fill time.
I4 Training clips are the last resort when intro footage is short.
I5 Stylised atmosphere clips (fireworks, fans with flags, stadium, trophy ceremony) are allowed to fill the intro.
I6 Pace: about 8 clips of 1.1-4.0 s (median 2.6 s) for a 20 s intro.

intro_to_main: T1 End the intro on a close-up of the player.
T2 Switch with a quick push-in with blur on the last 0.15 s, then a hard cut (transition=zoom_punch_cut on the first main shot).
T3 The first main shot is a wide clip of 0.6-1.2 s, immediately followed by the close-up part of the same action.

rules: M1 Cut mostly on hard cuts. Median clip 3.5 s, 10th to 90th percentile 1.6-6.7 s, longest 9 s.
M2 Rhythm: 2-4 close or semi-close skill clips, then 1-3 wide clips, then repeat.
M3 Skill clips are dribbling, ball receiving, passing, run-making and 1v1 duels. Run-making counts as a skill clip.
M4 Wide clips of the player must be chosen so the cut looks like a match cut (similar position, direction and action as the clip before or after).
M5 Look for match-up cuts between clips and place those clips together.
M6 Goals: 1-3 goal clips spread through the main part. If the sources have none, use none. Show the first goal (or a worthwhile near miss) between 0:30 and 1:30 of the video.
M7 Cut a long goal clip into short parts and arrange the parts (build-up, shot, finish) instead of playing it whole.
M8 If a penalty goal exists, use one in the main part.
M9 Show 1-2 face clips of the player, only if needed.
M10 Sometimes include a good pass or a chance the player created.
M11 Wide clips stay at or below 25% of main (target about 20%).
M12 Speed is 1.0 unless a clip would otherwise be too short.
O1 Use after-match or celebration clips.
O2 If a clip of the player going into the tunnel exists, end the video on it.
O3 Pace: about 5 clips of 1.5-5.0 s (median 3.3 s).

never: Do not output any key other than the schema keys.
Do not invent files, shot types or timestamps.
Do not exceed the source length.
Do not add title text, captions or end cards.

pacing_fingerprint.note: Measured clip lengths in seconds from the reference edit, in playback order. The offline fallback planner samples from these.
